title: Pawn breaks
summary: Pawn breaks open lines: ...c5 against d4, e4 in the centre. In the Advance Caro-Kann, hit the base of the chain.
body:
### Break the pawn chain

A pawn break is a pawn move that attacks an enemy pawn. It opens lines for your pieces. Most plans in the opening and the middlegame end with a break.

A pawn chain is a diagonal line of pawns. Each pawn guards the pawn diagonally ahead of it. The base is the pawn at the back. Attack the base of a chain. In the Advance Caro-Kann, White has pawns on d4 and e5. The pawn on d4 is the base. Black plays ...c5 to hit it. In the Slav and Semi-Slav, White has the chain e3-d4, and d4 is the head. The same break ...c5 still hits d4 and opens the c-file.

White has breaks too. In the Semi-Slav and in many London positions, White plays e3-e4 to open the centre.

Ask three questions before a break:

- Are my pieces ready? A break needs pieces behind it.
- What does it open? A file or diagonal must help me, not my opponent.
- Is there a better break? A break can fail. Check what your opponent can do after it.

A break that comes too early can lose a pawn. A break that comes too late can be stopped. Look for the right moment.

After the break, look at what your opponent does. He can take, push past, or ignore it. Check each answer before you play.

Rule of thumb: attack the base of the chain with a pawn break when your pieces are ready.

exercises.prompt: Black to move. White has pawns on d4 and e5. Hit the base of the chain with a pawn.
exercises.explanation: The chain is d4-e5. The base is d4. ...c5 attacks it, even though c3 guards it. The other pawn break, ...f6, hits the head of the chain on e5, so it does not fit the prompt. One line is ...c5 Be2 Nc6, and White castles. Other moves, such as ...a6, are only a little worse.

exercises.prompt: Black to move. White has played Bf4. Hit the pawn on d4 with your c-pawn.
exercises.explanation: ...c5 attacks d4. Only the knight on f3 and the queen guard it. One line is ...c5 e3 Nc6 Nbd2 cxd4 Nxd4 e6. ...e6 is almost as good, about the same win %, because it prepares ...c5 too. The prompt asks for the c-pawn, so only ...c5 fits.

exercises.prompt: White to move. Break in the centre with your e-pawn.
exercises.explanation: e4 attacks the bishop on f5 and the pawn on d5 at once. The pawn on c4 is weak. If the bishop moves, exd5 follows, and Nxc4 wins the pawn on c4. In the line ...Bxe4 Nxe4 dxe4 d5, the pawn attacks the knight on c6, and White also threatens Bxc4 to win the pawn on c4. Every Black reply gives White a clear edge. f3 prepares e4, but it is slow: after ...Bg6 the bishop is safe and the break wins nothing. The engine rates f3 about 48 %, and e4 about 61 %.

exercises.prompt: White to move. Break in the centre with your e-pawn.
exercises.explanation: e4 fights for the centre. One line is e4 e5 cxd5 cxd5 Re1 Re8. Re1 prepares e4. c5 gains space on the queenside. Both are almost as good. The prompt asks for the e-pawn, so only e4 fits.
